events.title: Julius Caesar arrives in Egypt and learns of Pompey's death
events.description: Julius Caesar, pursuing Pompey, arrived at Alexandria, capital of Ptolemaic Egypt, and learned of his rival's death. Kept there by the Etesian winds, he went on to arbitrate the civil war between the child pharaoh Ptolemy XIII and Cleopatra.

events.title: Theophilos succeeds his father Michael II as Byzantine emperor
events.description: On the death of Michael II, first ruler of the Amorian dynasty, his son Theophilos became Byzantine emperor. He reigned until 842, fought the Abbasids, and was the last emperor to support iconoclasm.

events.title: Otto I crushes the rebels at the Battle of Andernach
events.description: At Andernach on the Rhine, followers of King Otto I of Germany decisively defeated rebels led by Eberhard of Franconia, the brother of the late King Conrad I. The rebel leaders were killed, and Franconia came directly under the crown.

events.title: Saladin takes Jerusalem from the Crusaders
events.description: After a short siege, Saladin accepted the surrender of Jerusalem, ending 88 years of Crusader rule. Most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves, and the city's loss prompted the Third Crusade.

events.title: Scots and Norwegians fight the Battle of Largs
events.description: On the Ayrshire coast near Largs, Scots fought part of the storm-battered fleet of Haakon IV of Norway, who sought to reassert Norwegian sovereignty over Scotland's western seaboard. Haakon withdrew, and in 1266 his successor ceded the Hebrides and Man to Scotland.

events.title: Major John André is hanged as a British spy
events.description: Major John André, captured carrying Benedict Arnold's plans to surrender West Point, was hanged at Tappan, New York. His composure won sympathy even among his captors, while Arnold's name became a byword for treason.

events.title: Texan settlers fire the first shots of the Texas Revolution
events.description: At Gonzales, Texan colonists refused to hand back a small cannon to Mexican troops and fired on them beneath a flag reading 'Come and Take It'. The skirmish opened the war that led to Texan independence in 1836.

events.title: Mohandas Gandhi is born in Porbandar
events.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in Porbandar, on India's western coast. His method of non-violent mass resistance, satyagraha, drove the Indian independence movement and inspired civil rights campaigns worldwide.

events.title: Mexican troops open fire on students at Tlatelolco
events.description: Soldiers and police fired on a student rally in Mexico City's Plaza de las Tres Culturas, ten days before the Olympic Games opened. Estimates of the dead range from about 30 to several hundred; the government long concealed the toll.
